title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 01 (Narration & Voice Focus)
subject: english-10

questions.question: He said, "I am busy now." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He said that he was busy then.
options.B: He said that he is busy now.
options.C: He said he was busy now.
options.D: He said that he had been busy then.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ('said'), the present simple tense ('am') shifts to past simple ('was'), and the time adverb 'now' shifts to 'then'.

questions.question: She said, "I finished my work yesterday." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She said she finished her work the previous day.
options.B: She said she has finished her work yesterday.
options.C: She said that she had finished her work the previous day.
options.D: She said she finishes her work the previous day.

questions.explanation: Past simple tense ('finished') shifts to past perfect tense ('had finished'), and the time adverb 'yesterday' shifts to 'the previous day' or 'the day before'.

questions.question: He said, "I will go tomorrow." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He said he would go the next day.
options.B: He said he will go tomorrow.
options.C: He said he would go tomorrow.
options.D: He said he goes the next day.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'will' shifts to 'would' in indirect reporting, and the time expression 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.

questions.question: She said, "I have been reading this book." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She said she has been reading that book.
options.B: She said that she had been reading that book.
options.C: She said she was reading that book.
options.D: She said she read that book.

questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous tense ('have been reading') shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been reading'), and the demonstrative pronoun 'this' shifts to 'that'.

questions.question: The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
options.B: The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
options.C: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
options.D: The teacher told that the sun is rising in the east.

questions.explanation: Universal truths, scientific facts, and habitual actions do not undergo tense backshift even when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

questions.question: She said to me, "Where are you going?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She asked me where was I going.
options.B: She asked me where I was going.
options.C: She asked me where am I going.
options.D: She told me where I was going.

questions.explanation: In indirect interrogative sentences beginning with Wh-words, the reporting verb changes to 'asked', the Wh-word acts as conjunction, and the sentence order becomes assertive (subject before auxiliary: 'I was going').

questions.question: He said to her, "Do you like coffee?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He asked her that did she like coffee.
options.B: He asked her if she liked coffee.
options.C: He told her whether she likes coffee.
options.D: He asked her whether did she like coffee.

questions.explanation: For Yes/No interrogative sentences, the reporting clause connects with 'if' or 'whether', the auxiliary 'do' is removed, and the verb shifts to past simple ('liked').

questions.question: The doctor said to the patient, "Take your medicine regularly." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The doctor advised the patient to take his medicine regularly.
options.B: The doctor said the patient that he should take his medicine regularly.
options.C: The doctor ordered the patient take his medicine regularly.
options.D: The doctor asked the patient taking medicine regularly.

questions.explanation: In imperative sentences expressing medical counsel, the reporting verb becomes 'advised', and the imperative verb is converted into a to-infinitive clause ('to take').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Ali wrote an essay yesterday.'

options.A: An essay was written by Ali yesterday.
options.B: An essay had been written by Ali yesterday.
options.C: An essay is written by Ali yesterday.
options.D: An essay has been written by Ali yesterday.

questions.explanation: Past simple tense in active voice ('wrote') changes into 'was/were + past participle' ('was written') in passive voice.

questions.question: Select the correct active voice of: 'The car is being washed by the driver.'

options.B: The driver was washing the car.
options.C: The driver is washing the car.
options.D: The driver has washed the car.

questions.explanation: 'is being washed' is present continuous passive, which corresponds to the present continuous active form 'is washing'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is in the PASSIVE voice?

options.A: The gardener pruned the rose bushes this morning.
options.B: The committee has evaluated all applications.
options.C: The historical monument was restored by renowned architects.
options.D: The birds will migrate south before winter.

questions.explanation: Option C features the passive auxiliary 'was restored' with the agent introduced by the prepositional phrase 'by renowned architects'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The students are preparing a science exhibition.'

options.A: A science exhibition was being prepared by the students.
options.B: A science exhibition is prepared by the students.
options.C: A science exhibition is being prepared by the students.
options.D: A science exhibition has been prepared by the students.

questions.explanation: Present continuous active ('are preparing') converts to 'is/am/are being + past participle' ('is being prepared').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'They had announced the results before sunset.'

options.A: The results have been announced by them before sunset.
options.B: The results had been announced by them before sunset.
options.C: The results were announced by them before sunset.
options.D: The results had announced before sunset.

questions.explanation: Past perfect active ('had announced') changes into 'had been + past participle' ('had been announced') in passive voice.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the imperative sentence: 'Open the window.'
questions.explanation: Imperative commands are converted into passive using the formula: 'Let + object + be + past participle' ('Let the window be opened').

questions.question: Convert into passive voice: 'Do not pluck the flowers.'

options.A: Let the flowers not be plucked.
options.B: The flowers are not to pluck.

questions.explanation: Negative imperatives take the passive form 'Let + object + not + be + past participle' ('Let the flowers not be plucked').
